# API reference — Rust generic seam

<!-- generated by examples/gen_api_doc.py from the built module's docstrings - do not edit -->

The Rust core owns the shared optimization seam. Python callers reach it through `mltreelib.solvers.optimize`. Guide: [Generic optimizer](../../examples/generic-optimizer.md).

Reach the module through `mltreelib_core::generic` or `mltreelib_core::solver::generic`. The short names `Bounds`, `Budget`, `Constraint`, `ConstraintKind`, `Objective`, `ObjectiveError`, `OptimizationRequest`, `OptimizationResult`, `OptimizerKind`, `SmoothObjective`, and `SolveStatus` are re-exported from `mltreelib_core::solver`.

## solver/generic/bounds.rs

### Bounds

```rust
pub struct Bounds {
```

Lower and upper limits for each parameter.

A bound is either finite or infinite. `lower[i] <= upper[i]` holds for every dimension. A fully unbounded domain uses negative and positive infinity.

### Bounds.new

```rust
pub fn new(lower: Vec<f64>, upper: Vec<f64>) -> Result<Self, String> {
```

Builds bounds from per-dimension lower and upper limits.

Returns an error when the vectors differ in length, when a limit is `NaN`, when a lower limit is positive infinity, when an upper limit is negative infinity, or when a lower limit exceeds its upper limit.

### BudgetStatus


Which budget ended a run.

### Budget

```rust
pub struct Budget {
```

Counts user objective evaluations and solver iterations.

One counter covers every user objective call, including calls inside local solves, perturbation steps, population initialization, and archive updates.

### Budget.new

```rust
pub fn new(max_evaluations: Option<usize>, max_iterations: Option<usize>) -> Self {
```

Builds a budget with optional limits. `None` means unlimited.

### Constraint.new


Builds evaluated constraint values.

### violation

```rust
pub fn violation(kind: ConstraintKind, value: f64) -> f64 {
```

Largest violation of one constraint value.

An inequality value below zero violates the constraint by its magnitude. An equality value violates the constraint by its absolute distance from zero.

### max_violation

```rust
pub fn max_violation(kind: ConstraintKind, values: &[f64]) -> f64 {
```

Largest violation across all constraint values.

### is_feasible

```rust
pub fn is_feasible(kind: ConstraintKind, values: &[f64], tolerance: f64) -> bool {
```

Reports whether constraint values satisfy the constraint.

Inequality values accept a small negative slack. Equality values accept an absolute distance from zero up to the tolerance.

## solver/generic/mod.rs

### optimize

```rust
pub fn optimize(request: &OptimizationRequest) -> Result<OptimizationResult, String> {
```

Runs one optimization with the shared contracts.

The method dispatch resolves the method-specific options, evaluates the objective through one shared budget, and returns the shared result type. A method that is not implemented yet returns one error naming the method.

### Objective

```rust
pub trait Objective {
```

A bounded scalar objective.

Implementations return one finite value for one point. Solvers reject non-finite values through [`ObjectiveError::NotFinite`] and report the [`crate::solver::generic::SolveStatus::InvalidObjective`] status.

## solver/generic/random.rs

### latin_hypercube_samples

```rust
pub fn latin_hypercube_samples( bounds: &Bounds, samples: usize, seed: u64, ) -> Result<Vec<Vec<f64>>, String> {
```

Builds Latin hypercube samples inside finite bounds.

Every dimension is stratified independently into `samples` strata. One point takes one stratum per dimension. The stratum order is shuffled per dimension with the seeded generator.

### random_search

```rust
pub fn random_search( objective: &dyn Objective, budget: &mut Budget, options: &RandomSearchOptions, seed: u64, initial_population: Option<&[Vec<f64>]>, ) -> OptimizationResult {
```

Runs uniform random search inside bounds.

Candidates come from `initial_population` first when one is supplied. The remaining candidates are uniform draws.

### latin_hypercube_search


Runs Latin hypercube sampling inside bounds.

